meta.title: $80M Investor: You Have 5 Years Left To Get Rich
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · observational investing method · a leveraged risk bucket · the $10M Amazon earnings trade · AI's efficiency wave and robotics · Bitcoin as a wealth-transfer trade · the Take-Two GTA 6 watch

snapshot: Chris Camillo says he turned about **$20,000 into $80 million+** by spotting shifts in real life and on social media before Wall Street; audited by Jack Schwager and Business Insider.
His four steps: does it move a public company's needle, do investors already know, is anything bigger happening there, and when will others find out.
He argues for a separate high-risk bucket using options, margin or a 3x S&P ETF, with leverage reserved for high-conviction trades (75-80 in 18 years).
His Amazon earnings call options added **over $10 million** in a couple of days after he had been down almost 50%; he rated it an 80/20 bet.
Thesis: after Nvidia and infrastructure comes an **AI efficiency wave** that favors incumbents with distribution; Amazon has the biggest moat.
Holdings named: Amazon (still heavy, some leverage), **Bloom Energy**, Robinhood; Bitcoin as a bet on a $100 trillion+ wealth transfer.
He has opened a small long in **Take-Two (TTWO)** ahead of GTA 6, read through gamer comments, ready to sell or short as footage lands.
He gives individual investors about five years of edge before AI agents do this research too.

themes.title: Observational investing: spot the shift, then check if it moves a stock
themes.lead: Camillo argues markets stay inefficient because investors chase the same 20 companies and the Fed, while consumer shifts show up on TikTok first.
bullets: Origin: as a kid, a half-empty Snapple door at 7-Eleven (Arizona Iced Tea competition) led to **$300** of puts that tripled on Snapple's first bad quarter.

Four tests: does it move revenue, perception or cost for a public company; do institutional or retail investors already know; is something bigger happening at the company; when will others find out (release date, credit-card data, earnings call).
A viral TikTok bottled water failed test one: its owner had bigger brands, so it could not move the needle.
**Roof repair**: Google Trends searches ran about 3x the prior five years in a hail season, so he bet with options on Beacon Roofing ahead of the insurance report hedge funds pay for.
Past trades: Barbie, Lionsgate with The Hunger Games, every shoe trend in 20 years, 100% of his account in a Nintendo ADR after trying the Wii at E3.
He still spends 1-2 hours a day (down from four) in TikTok comments ('the gold is in the comments'), e.g. Chili's cheese pull; for AI he reads developer forums, Reddit and X.

LLMs now do the dot-connecting: ask ChatGPT, Claude or Grok to validate the trend, find exposed companies and check what is priced in; more than half his ideas come from his Dumb Money Live community.

quote.text: The magic is in the comments. The gold is in the comments.

themes.title: A separate leveraged bucket, funded by trade-offs, not savings
themes.lead: He says wealth gets built through leverage, but only with money you can afford to see drop 90%.
bullets: An option lets $100 control about 10x the stock: a 10-20% move can return 100-200%, a 5% drop can wipe it out; max loss is known, unlike margin.
Claim: a 3x leveraged S&P ETF returned about **15%** a year over 100 years versus 10%; $1 at 18 grows to about $50 by 60 unlevered versus $350 levered, so $100k becomes $3.5M not $700k.
He puts the odds of that 7x outcome at 99% by his research, accepting drawdowns of 50-90%.
Fund it from trade-offs (casino money, $18 bar drinks), never college or retirement money; analogy: you use a stove safely rather than never lighting fire at home.
Warning: kids buying far out-of-the-money options act like his son's friends on six-game parlays, and lose almost every time.
Trading costs used to be 2-3% each way, about 5% round trip, by phone; now free on Robinhood-style apps.

quote.text: There's a correct way to use fire. There's a correct way to use leverage.

themes.watch: The 15% leveraged-ETF figure is a simulated back-test he cites, not a fund's track record.

themes.title: The $10 million Amazon earnings trade
themes.lead: After losing on options that expired before earnings, he put about a third of what remained on one-day calls and won.
bullets: Account was down almost **50%** over a few weeks; the final bet was about 20% of the larger account, expiring in about a day.
Research was a 'matrix': developer sentiment, AWS compute spot pricing and contracts; he expected a beat above the ~25% whisper number.
The key was CEO Andy Jassy handling capex as Microsoft had days earlier: demand is real and much equipment spend can be delayed.
He rated it 80/20, with the 20% being things outside his control (White House, Iran, a surprise investment); he says he should have made it a $30M+ day; his previous best was $5M.
Context: the selloff before it came from the liquidation of Leopold's fund, which he calls artificial and mostly over.
A 1.2 million-view livestream of his call with a friend drew 'degenerate' criticism; he says it sat in an account built for risk.
He still holds Amazon heavily with some leverage, though no longer about 70% of the portfolio.

quote.text: You only gain conviction from the work you put in.

themes.title: AI's next wave favors incumbents with distribution; robots come slower than hyped
themes.lead: He sees AI as the biggest opportunity of his life, moving from Nvidia to infrastructure to an efficiency wave across all companies.
bullets: Phases: discovery (ChatGPT, Nvidia, his first AI win), infrastructure (still underway, 20-30 companies in chips, data centers, energy, memory), then the **efficiency wave**.
In the efficiency wave, incumbents with distribution and supply relationships win, because their AI agents innovate as fast as startups; that could lift the whole market.
He holds Palantir-type names, memory and data-center stocks, plus Japanese chip-testing equipment makers; he thinks compute stays scarce despite Chinese open models.
**Bloom Energy** is a big holding: the fastest way to power data centers now told to bring their own energy; volatile and misunderstood.
Robotics: the largest TAM on Earth, not winner-take-all, deployment slow like mainframes; Tesla in pole position but must execute (Optimus leadership churn); Apptronik and Figure AI also named.
Timing: a commercially scalable humanoid in **2027**, scaling from 2028, companies paying $70-100k a year to rent one; homes in 5-10 years.
He was an early investor in one of the big three robot companies eight years ago and says he backs nearly all of them.

themes.title: Bitcoin rides the wealth transfer; Robinhood and kids' accounts close the wealth gap
themes.lead: He doesn't care why people own Bitcoin, only that the young generation inheriting over $100 trillion does.
bullets: Bitcoin tailwind over the next **20-25 years** from a $100 trillion+ transfer to younger, crypto-minded investors; the only risk he sees is security concerns.
Same logic as gold, which he says had no reason to own for 40 years but rose as people believed in it.
**Robinhood**: best-managed financial institution, with a good shot at becoming the world's largest within 20 years.
The program giving every child a **$1,000** brokerage account is 'the most genius thing'; Dell and other donors are topping them up.
Fix the wealth gap, not the income gap: get everyone owning stocks; a Reagan-era idea to put 10% of Social Security in the market would have closed it.
About 40 million new US retail traders, half on X, mostly chasing the same 10 stocks; he would cut market hours to four.

themes.title: Take-Two and GTA 6: the launch is priced in, the living world is not
themes.lead: His sealed-envelope pick is a binary trade on whether GTA 6 delivers a world players never want to leave.
bullets: GTA 6, 13 years in the making, could be the biggest entertainment release ever; the whole company hinges on it.
The release is priced in; upside is monetization inside a truly immersive world. If not delivered, the stock is too high.
A hacker leaked gameplay daily (the game is digital-only); the stock dipped. First gameplay comes in a Netflix special.
He reads only ordinary gamers' comments, not investors'; consensus so far is more love than hate, so he went long.
He traded Take-Two on every GTA release before; he may add, sell or short hour by hour.

quote.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 is fully priced in. What is not priced in is the ultimate success or failure of the game.

takeaways.title: Run any trend through the four tests before buying: needle, known, bigger news, timing
Read the last 3-4 earnings transcripts to learn what actually moves a company
Size leverage only from a separate bucket you can watch fall 90%
Look past infrastructure to incumbents with distribution for the efficiency wave
Watch gamer sentiment on GTA 6 footage as the Take-Two signal

hot_takes.take: If you just become an investor, you've already won.
Most investors are lazy. They're just lazy.
I think at some point in 2027 we're going to have a commercially scalable humanoid.
I don't think there's any reason to invest in gold for the last 40 years.
I think the market should be open like four hours.
This is the biggest existential threat that I've seen to humanity ever since I've been alive.
hot_takes.why: AI safety view from a self-described optimist

claims.claim: A commercially scalable humanoid robot will exist in 2027, with scaling starting in 2028.
Humanoids reach homes in about 5-10 years.
Companies will pay $70-100k a year to rent a humanoid robot.
Robinhood has a good shot at becoming the world's largest financial institution within 20 years.
Bitcoin has a strong tailwind from the $100 trillion wealth transfer over 20-25 years.
Individual observational investors have about five years before AI agents erase the edge.
A leveraged S&P bucket has a 99% chance of a 7x higher outcome over a working life.

other_news.title: He made **more than $30 million** in COVID: Google-translated Chinese medical reports, shorted airlines and casinos (losing for weeks at ~10% a week), then bought work-from-home names two days after the bottom: HP printers, bikes, RVs, boats, Amazon, Shopify, Peloton, a Schwinn-owning Canadian firm (~10x). He gave back a chunk while distracted by NFTs.

Asked about superintelligence wiping out humanity, he says doomers could be right without action and labs and governments barely coordinate; his bigger fear is a bad actor using pre-ASI tools for mass destruction.

Most billionaires aren't happy; the sweet spot is financial independence, then put on the brakes. He gives most profits to his foundation (elder care, pediatric care, animal welfare) and plans to back Beast Philanthropy's push against child labor after a Ghana cacao trip with MrBeast.

Sold Collect-a-Con, the largest Pokemon convention, to Ari Emanuel; opening an Austin studio to build a woman creator's podcast; a non-investing Dumb Money spin-off is coming. Advice to the young: authentic relationships and creating content scale trust.

Sources referenced: Nassim Taleb's The Black Swan, Jack Schwager's Unknown Market Wizards, his own book Laughing at Wall Street (2010), Covestor, Business Insider, Google Trends, earnings-call transcripts.
